subject: PrivGPU onramp — throughput quantification & network fallback plan
messages:
From: Tim Carlson <tim.carlson@edgewave.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@edgewave.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivGPU onramp: throughput targets and fallback options

Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — EdgeWave is excited about the performance numbers. Before procurement and legal can sign off we need a short, concrete plan for the private GPU pool onramp. High level asks below:

- Peak throughput target: we need to support 15k tokens/s at peak for our inferencing burst windows (approx 10-15 minutes).
- Sustained baseline: ~4k tokens/s with p95 latency <250ms and p50 <120ms.
- Failure/fallback behavior: if private pool saturates, we need an automated fallback (either to hosted tier or queued requests) and clear SLAs for failover.
- Network constraints: our colo cross-connects are currently 10Gbps per pipe; if you recommend 40Gbps we need a cost/lead time estimate.
- Timeline: target go-live in 6 weeks from contract.

I've attached our sampled traffic profile for the last 30 days (edgewave_prod_traffic_profile.csv). Can you confirm what dedicated GPU count and networking you recommend, and which items will be contractually covered vs. optional? Also please point us to the SOC2 / audit artifacts procurement needs.

We'll loop procurement separately but wanted to start with the technical sizing so we can align on the Demo -> Onramp path.

Thanks,
Tim Carlson
Head of Platform
EdgeWave Systems

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Carlson <tim.carlson@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivGPU onramp: throughput targets and fallback options

Tim — thanks for the clear rundown and for the traffic sample, that helps a lot. High-level responses below; I'll follow up with a sizing estimate and an internal runbook we'd hand off to your SREs.

Summary answers (short):
- Dedicated pool: to meet 15k tokens/s peak with our standard batching + KV-cache strategy for the Llama-variant model you showed, initial recommendation is 8x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (conservative) with warm-pool capacity to absorb bursts.
- Sustained: with that pool we expect baseline 4k tokens/s easily at target latencies (p50 <120ms) if your egress is provisioned at >=30Gbps aggregated.
- Fallbacks: we support two automated patterns: 1) model-level graceful degradation (route to a lower-capacity quantized variant) and 2) spillover to Redwood hosted (rate-limited) with a circuit-breaker and alerting. We can contract the second as a paid fallback addendum.
- Network: cross-connect to a 40Gbps port is preferred for headroom; 30Gbps is workable with slight added latency during sustained bursts. We will estimate cost/week for cross-connect recommendations in the sizing worksheet.
- Timeline: 6 weeks is tight but doable if procurement signs the dedicated pool commit this week; otherwise 8-10 weeks for cross-connect provisioning and security onboarding.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) I'll attach a sizing workbook (privpool-sizing-estimate-v1.xlsx) with GPU counts, expected QPS, and egress numbers.
2) Markus (engineer) will add a short tradeoff note on warm-pool vs. instant-burst capacity.
3) We provide a SOC2 evidence packet and DocuSign template for fallback addendum for procurement.

On quoting your items: could you confirm whether your traffic profile represents peak overlapping windows (i.e., many users bursting simultaneously) or thinly distributed bursts? That will change the warm-pool sizing assumptions.

--
Naomi Feldman
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Tim Carlson <tim.carlson@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivGPU onramp: throughput targets and fallback options

Tim / Naomi / Alex — quick engineering note with tradeoffs and a draft sizing matrix. I've summarized the key capacity levers and conservative numbers. See sizing-matrix-notes.txt attached.

Key assumptions I used:
- Model: Llama-3-Chat-33B-like (medium KV cache hit rate assumed ~25% for your patterns).
- Preferred batch size: adaptive batching with 25-40ms scheduling window to keep latency low while aggregating tokens.
- GPU effective token throughput (conservative): 2k tokens/s per A100-80GB equiv for mixed-batch workloads.

Sizing summary (conservative):
- Sustained ~4k tokens/s -> 2 GPUs (2 x 2k = 4k) if traffic spreads evenly and cache hits are favorable.
- Peak 15k tokens/s -> 8 GPUs (8 x 2k = 16k) to keep headroom. We recommend reserving 2 additional warm GPUs (total 10) if you want <30s cold-warm ramp.

Network and egress:
- Estimated egress at peak: ~22-26 Gbps (model dependent and depends on avg tokens/resp). With TLS + FRAMING overhead budget 30 Gbps recommended; 40 Gbps preferred for future growth and multi-tenant bursts.
- Cross-connect: 40Gbps reduces queuing jitter and allows more aggressive batching without hitting NIC saturation. If constrained to 10Gbps pipes, we must shard across NICs and expect non-linear latency increases.

Fallbacks and contractual options:
- Option A (included): model-level fallback to quantized variant — no cross-region egress.
- Option B (paid addendum): Redwood-hosted spillover with SLA for acceptance and rate-limiting. DocuSign template attached in related links.

Operational recommendations:
- Warm-pool choreography: maintain 20% of pool as warm; warmup via low-priority background traffic during non-peak hours.
- Admission control: soft-threshold at 80% aggregate token throughput to trigger graceful degradation rules.
- Observability: token-level traces and per-route cost/latency dashboards (we will export a dashboard link you can share with SRE).

Deliverables I'll drop into the shared Drive: a small sizing workbook and a one-page network onramp checklist. Naomi: please confirm if we should include gpu thermal/placement constraints for your colo.

-Markus
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Thanks Naomi and Markus — that level of detail is helpful. Procurement, can you confirm what SOC2 artifacts you need? I'll have Tim add the network diagrams for the colo.

We are comfortable moving forward with the 8 GPU baseline + 2 warm GPUs (10 total) and we want the paid-hosted-spillover option as an emergency fallback. Please include the DocuSign fallback addendum and a line item for cross-connect provisioning (40Gbps preferred).

Procurement: please see attached SOC2 evidence request (SOC2-evidence-request.pdf) and route to the correct bucket.

Sarah Li
Program Manager, EdgeWave Systems
